content:
Many people with arthritis and frailty live in care homes. Pain is common but can be missed, especially in people with dementia or communication difficulties.

This guide explains what residents and families can ask for. It is educational information and does not replace advice from the home or health professionals.

Pain assessment and review

  • Pain should be assessed regularly, including using observation tools for people who cannot say they are in pain.
  • Ask for a review if behaviour changes, such as restlessness, refusing to move, or agitation, as these can be signs of pain.
  • Medicines should be reviewed regularly by a GP or pharmacist.
  • Nursing homes have registered nurses who can help with this.

Movement and activity

  • Encourage moving little and often within the person's ability.
  • Ask about physiotherapy or activity programmes.
  • Comfortable, supportive seating at the right height helps standing up.
  • Walking aids should be within reach and checked.

Meal times

  • Adapted cutlery, cups and plate guards can help painful hands.
  • Ask for help to be given with dignity at the person's pace.
  • Report weight loss, poor appetite or swallowing problems.

Raising concerns

Speak to the manager first. Care homes in England are regulated by the Care Quality Commission, in Wales by Care Inspectorate Wales, in Scotland by the Care Inspectorate and in Northern Ireland by RQIA.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

How can I tell if someone with dementia is in pain?

Look for changes in behaviour, facial expression, movement or sleep, and ask staff to use a pain assessment tool.

Can a care home resident see a physiotherapist?

Ask the home and GP about referral.

Who checks care home quality?

The national regulator in each UK nation.
